1 Purpose

Step 10 assembles verified outputs from Steps 00–09B into a Results and reproducibility package. It reuses saved estimates under the existing specification without further model estimation, resampling or NCT.

All comparisons remain descriptive unless an explicitly authorised formal test exists. No such cross-wave or education-group significance test is present in the current design. A regularised zero means that an edge was not retained by the selected procedure; it does not prove absence. Retained-edge count and global strength are not treated as ideological constraint.

5 Stage 4: current analysis scope

The current researcher-selected working title is:

Structural Differences in Selected Policy-Attitude Networks across U.S. Election Years: Evidence from ANES Samples, 2004–2024

The title and exact research-question wording still need to be entered into the formal decision log; supervisor confirmation remains advised. The completed outputs support:

  1. descriptive comparison of selected nine-node policy-attitude conditional- association networks in the 2004, 2012, 2016, 2020 and 2024 ANES analysis samples; and
  2. descriptive examination of corresponding edges and relational configurations within the two education groups in 2012, 2016, 2020 and

Expected Influence and Strength are exploratory, not separate confirmatory research questions.

All five primary networks produced the saved dense-network warning. Small retained edges therefore require particular caution. Edge count and global strength are reported as descriptive network quantities and are not equated with ideological constraint. The repeated cross-sectional design cannot identify individual change or causal ordering.

Five primary ANES analysis-sample networks using a common node order, layout and edge scale. Edges are descriptive conditional associations. No NCT or population-design-consistent comparison is implied.

Exploratory Expected Influence and auxiliary Strength. Lines connect repeated cross-sectional wave estimates for display only; no cross-wave centrality significance test was performed.

The core network-method claims are supported by Epskamp and Fried (2018), Epskamp, Borsboom and Fried (2018), Burger et al. (2023), and Bringmann et al. (2019), all of which have inspected local full text. The original Expected Influence definition is traced to Robinaugh, Millner and McNally (2016); the full text was inspected through an accessible PMC copy, but no local Zotero PDF is present. The qgraph software citation and official ANES documentation are also explicitly marked as absent from Zotero.
